title: Savings Hypotheses Board and Runbook for Mixed Workloads
creator: Priya Anand
description: Consolidate a prioritized hypotheses board and an operational runbook to systematically evaluate batching, KV-prefetch, and quantization strategies across heterogeneous customer workloads. Deliverables: (1) canonical hypotheses board (ranking, expected savings, risk, baseline tests), (2) experiment templates for field trials, (3) a step-by-step runbook for safe canary rollouts and automated rollback triggers, and (4) a decision log capturing trade-offs and final recommendations. Goal is to create a repeatable cadence that reduces signaled token cost by >=15% for medium-tail workloads while preserving latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Hypotheses board created and reviewed by Eng/Research/Console PMs with prioritized list (top 10) and expected median savings per hypothesis
3 experiment templates implemented and validated on staging (batching heuristics, kv-prefetch TTL profiles, int8 quant profile), with reproducible measurement harness
Runbook published in Confluence with execution checklist, monitoring dashboards, and rollback criteria; peer-reviewed and approved
Field trial plan with at least 2 customer cohorts and automated canary windows configured in Dedicated for safe ramping
updates: 2026-02-12: Ticket created after cross-functional kickoff. Initial problem statement and target metrics agreed (15% token cost reduction for tail workloads).

2026-02-19: Hypotheses workshop completed; generated 18 candidate interventions. Early sorting by deployment risk and expected upside. Added labels and assigned owners. Action: Eng to prototype batching heuristic.

2026-03-01: Eng prototype for adaptive batching submitted: PR github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821. Microbenchmarks show 9-12% token cost reduction on internal tail trace with 2–5% median latency increase — flagged for SLO analysis.

2026-03-05: Research validated KV-prefetch TTL heuristic on request traces; estimated 6% additional token savings if cache hit consistency maintained. Noted increased memory pressure during bursts; Eng to add eviction safety net.
2026-03-10: Quantization experiment plan (int8 + per-channel calibration) documented; concern from QA about hallucination drift for instruction-following prompts. QA assigned an evaluation suite.
comments: Jonah Brooks (Eng): 'Adaptive batching prototype looks promising but we need stricter latency SLO gates before any rollout. Suggest canary at 1% traffic with 95th percentile monitoring.'
Aisha Kapur (Research): 'KV-prefetch TTL tuning requires workload fingerprinting — some customers will get worse cache hit rates. Recommend per-customer profiles and a fallback to conservative TTL.'
Maya Li (Console PM): 'We should add a cost dashboard tile that surfaces per-route token delta during experiments so customers can opt into trials.'
Marco Reyes (Assignee): 'Action: wire up the experiment harness to metrics cluster and create alerting runbooks. ETA for harness: 2 weeks.'
risk_and_mitigation: Primary risks: latency SLO regressions, customer-visible quality regressions, and increased memory/GPU pressure. Mitigations: strict canary windows, automated rollback triggers based on 95p latency and generation-quality eval thresholds, per-customer opt-in, and a staged memory-capacity test before fleet rollout.
metrics: Target token-cost reduction (median across selected cohorts): 15%
Maximum allowed 95th percentile latency regression: 5% relative to baseline
Quality regression tolerance (eval suite pass-rate delta): <=2 percentage points
Field-trial adoption target: 2 pilot customers by end of Q2
